content: 1. Aquatic Plant Toxicity Testing: A toxicity test using Lemna spp. (duckweed) is recommended as a Tier I study to evaluate the effects on aquatic plants. If the Tier I study shows a detrimental effect of 50% or more, further Tier II testing is recommended using the same species. 2. Terrestrial Vascular Plant Testing: Seedling emergence and vegetative vigor tests are required at Tier I and Tier II levels. Tier II testing is recommended if Tier I results indicate a detrimental effect of 25% or more. These tests are particularly relevant for herbicides, desiccants, and defoliants. 3. Test Notes: Testing is not recommended for contained pesticide treatments (e.g., bait boxes, pheromone traps) unless adverse effects are reported. Testing is not required for known phytotoxicants unless they are herbicides or similar products. Testing is generally not recommended for granular formulations unless specific concerns arise. 4. Registration of Formulated Pesticide Products: Data requirements for registering formulated pesticide products are additional to those for active substances. Testing is typically conducted on the formulated product itself. 5. Testing may be waived for gases or highly volatile liquids. This includes scenarios where pesticides are applied to turfgrass, plant foliage, or soil. 6. Epidemiological Data: Human activity data is recommended if default or generic data are insufficient to demonstrate safe use. Protocols for such studies should be approved before initiation. 7. Environmental Fate and Behavior: Monitoring data on the fate and behavior of active substances and their metabolites are recommended if ecotoxicity data or literature indicate potential hazards to biota. Testing may include bioaccumulation studies, chronic toxicity in freshwater invertebrates, and long-term toxicity in fish. 8. Biochemical Pesticides: For biochemical pesticides, testing is generally conducted on the active substance, but field studies may use a typical end-use product for scientific relevance. Data requirements include identity, composition, physical and chemical properties, and analytical methods for residue determination. 9. Additional Notes: Testing requirements may be waived if the substance belongs to a well-characterized group with known toxicity profiles. Data on residue dissipation from treated surfaces (e.g., turfgrass, plant foliage) are recommended when pesticides are applied to such areas. For occupational sites, data are required if workers are likely to have post-application dermal contact with treated surfaces during typical activities. 10. Case-by-Case Recommendations:
